<action type="say">
For Riverwalk Court, here’s how I’d approach it for a business trip.

Best room type to target
- Primary pick: Standard King Room (or any “King” room on a higher/business floor).
  - Typically has the most straightforward desk/workspace setup.
  - Good for 1–2 adults if you don’t specifically need two beds.
- Consider upgrade if within budget: any room labeled “Executive,” “Business,” “Club Level,” or “River View Suite” that:
  - Shows a separate sitting area with a real desk and chair.
  - Is on a higher floor.  
- Choose Double Queen only if you truly need two beds; these sometimes sacrifice desk space.

On Booking.com, when you’re on the Riverwalk Court page:

1) Check the exact room type
- Open the room you’re considering and:
  - Read the description: look for “desk,” “work desk,” “seating area,” “armchair,” “business facilities,” “free WiFi in all rooms.”
  - Scan amenities list for: “Free WiFi,” “Desk,” “Coffee machine,” “Air conditioning.”
- Look closely at room photos:
  - Confirm a proper desk or large table (not just a tiny round side table).
  - Check for a real chair you can sit in for a few hours.
  - Look for outlets or lamps with power near the desk/bed.

2) Validate wifi + quiet via reviews
- On the Reviews tab:
  - Filter/sort to show the most recent reviews.
  - Use keywords: “wifi,” “internet,” “business trip,” “quiet,” “noise.”
  - You want recent mentions like “good wifi,” “great for work,” “quiet room/floor,” and avoid many “thin walls,” “street noise,” or “noisy hallway” comments.

3) Optimize for quiet (at booking time)
- In the room selection step, see if Booking offers free preferences like:
  - “Higher floor,” “Quiet room,” “Away from lift/elevator” — tick these if available.
- In the “Special requests” box, add something concise like:
  - “Business trip – if possible, high floor, quiet room away from elevator/ice machine and bar areas. Thank you.”
- After booking, you can also:
  - Message the property via the Booking.com app/website with the same request.

4) Double-check policies and costs
- Cancellation: Confirm free cancellation deadline (date & time) matches your risk tolerance.
- WiFi: Make sure it’s free in rooms (not just public areas).
- Extra fees: Look for any “property fee,” “resort/facility fee,” or mandatory charges in the price breakdown.
- Check-in/out times: Ensure they work with your flight schedule; note if you might need early check-in/late checkout.

If you want, paste the exact room names you’re seeing for Riverwalk Court on Booking (e.g., “Standard King – High Floor,” “Executive King Room – River View”), and I’ll tell you which one I’d choose and in what order. </action>

User has four room types at Riverwalk Court and wants a primary and backup choice optimized for workspace and quiet. Based on typical hotel patterns, Executive King with Lounge Access is best for business travelers, then King River View – High Floor, followed by King City View, with Double Queen City View last. I’ll rank them and give brief justifications plus quick checks and a suggested special request.
</think>
<plan>
1. Rank the four room types by suitability for work setup and quiet, with short reasons.
2. Suggest what to verify on Booking (desk, reviews).
3. Provide a concise special-request phrase to maximize quiet.
</plan>
<action type="say">
Here’s how I’d prioritize those for a business trip with your goals (workspace + quiet):

1) Executive King Room – Lounge Access  ← best choice  
- Why: “Executive” floors are usually designed for business travelers:
  - More likely to have a proper desk and chair.
  - Often on higher, quieter floors with fewer families/tour groups.
  - Lounge access gives you an extra quiet space to work/take calls.

2) King Room – River View – High Floor  ← strong backup  
- Why:
  - “High Floor” is excellent for quiet (less street/River Walk/bar noise).
  - Standard King layout usually includes a usable desk/workspace.
  - Great if Executive is sold out or the price jump isn’t worth it to you.

3) King Room – City View  
- Similar to the regular King layout, decent for work, but not guaranteed on the higher/quietest floors the way “High Floor”/Executive are.

4) Double Queen Room – City View  
- Last choice unless you truly need two beds:
  - Double-queen layouts sometimes compromise desk space.
  - Often attract more families/groups = potentially more hallway noise.

Before you book on Booking.com, quickly:

1) Open Executive King and River View – High Floor:
   - Check photos for:
     - A real desk or good-sized table.
     - A chair that looks usable for a few hours of work.
   - Confirm “Free WiFi in rooms” in the amenities text.

2) Scan recent reviews:
   - Filter/sort by newest.
   - Use keywords: “wifi,” “internet,” “business trip,” “quiet,” “noise.”
   - You want: solid wifi comments, and no pattern of “thin walls,” “noisy hallways,” or “loud bar.”

Special request text (paste into the “Requests” box when booking):
- “Business trip – if possible, a quiet room on a high floor, away from the elevator and ice machine. Thank you.”

If you share the price difference between Executive King and the River View – High Floor King, I can give you a quick “worth it / not worth it” judgment from a business-comfort perspective.</action>
